summary: Breakwater light at Grand Marais on Lake Superior's North Shore, first shown in 1885; the keeper's house is now a county historical museum.

lens.where: Cook County Historical Society museum, Grand Marais

structures.type: square pyramidal wooden tower with octagonal lantern

structures.note: In place 1920; moved along the breakwater that year and returned to the end of the eastern breakwater by 1922
Now the Cook County Historical Society museum

access.note: Coast Guard owned. Tower closed. The breakwater can be walked to view the light. The U.S. Lighthouse Society archive lists the station as not open to the public.

events.note: Light and fog bell began 1 September 1885; the Globe reported the lighthouse erected during the 1885 season
Storm-tossed seas breached the base of the exposed tower in November; repaired
Severe October storm damaged the tower; a plank protection was added on the east side
Keeper's dwelling completed (October 1896 per LighthouseFriends; built 1896 per the Cook County Historical Society)
Square pyramidal metal tower lit on 27 August 1904, replacing the post light placed on the breakwater in 1902
Storm of Monday 10 November 1919 nearly wrecked the tower; the sea tore holes in its south and north walls
Steel tower moved sixty yards east along the breakwater on 1 November 1920
Tower returned to the end of the eastern breakwater after a War Department permit in October 1922
Fog signal changed to an electric siren on 4 October 1923
Illuminant changed from oil gas to acetylene; light changed from fixed to flashing
Fog signal blast altered to five seconds every thirty-five seconds
Remote control under Public Works Administration funds: duplicate horn fog signal and electric light with lamp changer
Keeper's house acquired by the Cook County Historical Society
Keeper's house listed on the National Register of Historic Places (the light itself is not stated to be listed)

corrections.why: No source checked here dates a Grand Marais light structure to 1897. LighthouseFriends dates the wooden tower to 1885, the metal tower to 1904 and the steel tower to 1920.

corrections.proposed: 1920 for the steel tower (the first tower was wooden, finished 1885)
corrections.why: LighthouseFriends dates the wooden first tower to August 1885 and the steel tower to 1920 (in place that year). The archive's own record gives the tower as steel, pyramidal, built with the light; the steel tower is not the 1886 structure.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record gives 1922, 1897 and 1885. The 1922 date is the steel tower returned to the breakwater (LighthouseFriends), not the first light. The 1897 date has no source here. The first light was 1885, supported by the 1885 act, the Globe, and LighthouseFriends and the archive. The Cook County Historical Society's 1884 date is not supported by the other sources here.
The Cook County Historical Society says 1884; LighthouseFriends and the archive say 1885; the Globe says the lighthouse was erected in the past season of 1885. We follow 1885 and say so in the story.

notes_for_editor: Same name, different place: Grand Marais, Michigan (Grand Marais Harbor of Refuge, Alger County, Lake Superior; the NPS Cultural Landscapes report cli-grand-marais-uscg-ls-2020.pdf, Otto Buffe as keeper, the 1895 $4,000 item 'Grand Marais light-station, Michigan') is a different station. None of it is used here. The 1895 $4,000 act for the Minnesota dwelling rests on LighthouseFriends alone; no Minnesota primary for it was found in the corpus. The 1896 dwelling date rests on LighthouseFriends and the Cook County Historical Society. The archive prints two Mayhew lines for 1886 and starts him in 1886, while LighthouseFriends says he was first keeper at the 1885 lighting: check a NARA keeper register. The Lighthouse Board 1893 page number (p. 155) comes from the OCR header; scan page 212 is the citable page; check the image. The 1915 Commissioner printed page 38 is an OCR estimate. The 1925 and 1935 Bulletin pages are PDF pages. Breakwater: the 1915 Commissioner list says West Breakwater; LighthouseFriends says the 1920 move was along the eastern breakwater; not reconciled. Lit status: the archive says not an active aid to navigation; other records differ; not checked against a current Light List. Focal height and characteristic are in the station record (ENC, Light List) and were not checked here; the archive gives a lantern height of 38 ft (11.6 m) above mean high water, which does not match the 14.6 m in the record. Staffing and the date of automation were not found beyond keepers to at least 1946. No wreck or rescue tied to this light was found in the corpus or in the Chronicling America searches. Wikipedia gives 1922 as first lit and is not cited. Possible further sources: the Cook County News-Herald for 1885-1904 (not searched), Lighthouse Board annual reports for 1886-1892 and 1896-1904 (not in the local corpus). Fact-check 2026-10-28: the 1893 Board page is cited by scan page 212 only, because the corpus index reads the printed page as p.154? and the story no longer cites p.155. The 1935 control-circuit sentence is on PDF p.21 (footnote now pp.20-21). The word 'village' and the NARA attribution were removed (no cited page gives them; LighthouseFriends calls the place a city). The archive's 'Active Aid to Navigation: No' is reported as the archive's entry, not as a change of status.
